title: Normalized signed finite Tate maps and Kummer exponent compatibility
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $f:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Fix $m\geq1$ with $\ell^mA=\ell^mB=0$. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use constant coefficient and module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $R=A,B$ and $n\geq m$, put $L_{R,n}=\mu_{\ell^n,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T}R_T$, using the actual roots-of-unity sheaf [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Set $L_{R,n}^{[0]}=R_T$, $L_{R,n}^{[d]}=L_{R,n}^{\otimes d}$ for $d>0$, and $L_{R,n}^{[-d]}=\mathcal Hom_{R_T}(L_{R,n}^{[d]},R_T)$, with tensor and internal Hom as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. These are invertible lines [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free].

For each $n\geq m$ there is exactly one family of additive $f$-semilinear sheaf maps $c_{f,n}^r:L_{A,n}^{[r]}\to L_{B,n}^{[r]}$ ($r\in\mathbf Z$) with the following normalization on local sections: $c_{f,n}^0=f$, $c_{f,n}^1(z\otimes a)=z\otimes f(a)$, positive-degree maps are tensor powers of $c_{f,n}^1$, and, for $d>0$,
$$c_{f,n}^{-d}(\lambda)\bigl(c_{f,n}^{d}(x)\bigr)=f\bigl(\lambda(x)\bigr).$$
The induced $B_T$-linear map $\widetilde c_{f,n}^r:L_{A,n}^{[r]}\otimes_{A_T}B_T\to L_{B,n}^{[r]}$, $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,c_{f,n}^r(x)$, is an isomorphism.

For $n\geq k\geq m$ there is exactly one family of $R_T$-linear isomorphisms $e_R^{n,k,r}:L_{R,n}^{[r]}\to L_{R,k}^{[r]}$ whose degree-one map is $z\otimes a\mapsto z^{\ell^{n-k}}\otimes a$, whose degree-zero map is the identity, whose positive maps are tensor powers, and whose negative maps satisfy $e_R^{n,k,-d}(\lambda)(e_R^{n,k,d}(x))=\lambda(x)$. They satisfy $e_R^{n,n,r}=\mathrm{id}$ and $e_R^{k,j,r}e_R^{n,k,r}=e_R^{n,j,r}$ for $n\geq k\geq j\geq m$. Moreover the normalized families satisfy
$$e_B^{n,k,r}\circ c_{f,n}^r=c_{f,k}^r\circ e_A^{n,k,r}.$$
Equivalently, after ordinary scalar extension, $e_B^{n,k,r}\circ\widetilde c_{f,n}^r=\widetilde c_{f,k}^r\circ(e_A^{n,k,r}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{B_T})$.
